answer: Registration consumes a verifiable delay chain bound to the claimant key: the client walks a sequential hash from a fixed nadir seed to a depth set by current enrollment, about thirty minutes of single-core work. No cluster parallelises that ordering, and every leaf re-derives from the live epoch seed, so a thousand aliases cost a thousand serial runs plus their power. An honest solo operator starts near the nadir of that curve and reaches its zenith only when enrollments spike, pricing farms out first. A sampling watchdog, the falcon, voids any chain whose leaf predates the seed.
